item.title: Immigration sets 5 targets for new Comptrollers, as IGP seeks stronger partnership
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Comptroller General of the Nigeria Immigration Service NIS, Kemi Nandap, has set five “non-negotiable” expectations for newly promoted Comptrollers, ordering them to lead by example, deliver measurable results, protect the Service’s integrity, embrace reforms and develop their personnel. The Inspector General of Police IGP, Olatunji Disu, also pledged the Nigeria Police Force’s commitment to a stronger partnership with the Service. Both spoke on Thursday at the decoration of 94 new Comptrollers of Immigration. A total of 106 officers were promoted, but 12 retired before the ceremony. Nandap told the officers that their new rank came with heavier demands. “Promotion is not simply a reward for what you have accomplished. It is a declaration of confidence in what you are now expected to do,” she said. She said the rank was “a greater burden of trust” and a higher standard of conduct. “I have some expectations of you, and they are non-negotiable. First, you must lead by example. Two, you must deliver measurable results. Thirdly, protect the integrity of the service. Fourth, embrace innovation and institutional reforms. Change starts with you. Your attitude matters. And lastly, number five, develop your people. You must build competent and motivated and disciplined teams that are capable of sustaining progress of the service”, she demanded. The Comptroller General said the expectations were not ceremonial. “They are practical standards against which your leadership should be assessed. And I urge you to personally hold yourself accountable,” she said. She told the officers that the Service needed more than senior officers. It needs more effective leaders, Nandap said. “Corruption, extortion, abuse of office, professional negligence, and indiscipline have no place in the Nigerian immigration service we have built here. I expect every controller to demonstrate zero tolerance for misconduct. You cannot demand integrity from your subordinates while compromising your own principles”, she added. According to her, ongoing reforms were meant to make the Service professional, intelligence-led and technologically enabled. She cited the e-Border Solution, the Border Control and Immigration Management System (BCIMS) and the e-Gates among the digital platforms being deployed. But she cautioned that technology alone would not deliver results. “Our technology, no matter how sophisticated, cannot compensate for weak leadership, poor information, indiscipline, or the lack of accountability,” she said. She told the Comptrollers to ensure the reforms reached commands, border posts and airports. “You must take ownership of the systems entrusted to your formations. You must ensure that officers are properly trained,” she said. item.title: Carrick the fall guy for deeper problems at Man Utd – Report
item.description: Michael Carrick is the latest in a long line of managers to be sacked by Manchester United as they struggle to recapture former glories, but their problems run far deeper than the dugout. For the first time in 40 years, the 20-time English champions find themselves in the Premier League relegation zone at this stage of the season. Carrick was handed the job on a permanent basis fewer than six months ago after revitalising the team following the acrimonious departure of Ruben Amorim in January. Under the 45-year-old, then operating as interim boss, United finished third in the Premier League, securing a return to the Champions League after two seasons away. But the optimism quickly vanished at the start of this season and for the third consecutive campaign, woeful results have forced United into a mid-season managerial change. The Red Devils have won just three of their opening 15 games in all competitions. Carrick joins David Moyes, Louis van Gaal, Jose Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Erik ten Hag and Amorim among the managers who have struggled to arrest United’s overall decline, despite the occasional trophy, since Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. The Scot stepped down after collecting his 13th Premier League winner’s medal, at the end of a period of dominance in English football and European success. Now United, almost unbelievably, find themselves in a battle just to stay in the English top flight, where they have been ever-present for more than 50 years. USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino — the hot favourite to replace Carrick — faces the task of uniting a deeply divided club on and off the pitch. United captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped last month after he criticised Carrick’s tactics following a 4-1 humbling by Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez took a public swipe at the United hierarchy for not doing more to strengthen the squad in the summer transfer window. Carrick’s role as a player in the glory days under Ferguson meant he retained support among the fanbase despite a string of substandard displays. – Blame game – The anger of the supporters is instead firmly directed towards the club’s owners, whom they hold responsible for overseeing United’s slide. Despite fierce and persistent protests over two decades, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club, which Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts. Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have since faded. Ratcliffe, founder and chairman of industrial giant INEOS, has overseen cost-cutting measures, including widespread redundancies, and hiked up ticket prices, but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.46 billion). Former United captain Gary Neville has lamented the “inept” ownership and leadership of his boyhood club. item.title: Reps move to establish national research, innovation fund
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has moved to establish a National Research and Innovation Development Fund to address funding gaps, strengthen Nigeria’s research capacity and promote the commercialisation of locally developed innovations. The proposed legislation also seeks to establish a National Council on Research and Innovation to provide a legal and institutional framework for coordinating research activities, supporting scientific discoveries and transforming research outcomes into marketable products and services. Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, disclosed this on Thursday at a public hearing organised by the House Committee on Science and Technology on the National Research and Innovation Development Fund and National Council on Research and Innovation Bill, 2026 (HB. 2821), at the National Assembly, Abuja. Represented by the Deputy House Leader, Abubakar Halims, Abbas said Nigeria could no longer afford to depend excessively on imported technologies and solutions to challenges its citizens had the intellectual capacity to address. He noted that despite the country’s considerable intellectual resources, talented researchers, innovative young people and skilled entrepreneurs, the absence of an effective system linking research to funding and industry had continued to limit the economic benefits of these capabilities. According to him, research activities in Nigeria often end with academic publications, while promising innovations struggle to attract financing and discoveries with commercial potential fail to progress beyond the laboratory. “The challenge, therefore, is not simply to produce more research, but to build an ecosystem that connects research to funding, innovation to investment, and discoveries to industry,” the Speaker said. He added that the objective of the public hearing was not merely to defend the Bill in its current form but to ensure that the proposed legislation could effectively achieve its intended purpose. Earlier, Chairman of the House Committee on Science and Technology, Zakariya Tijjani Zannah, said Nigeria possessed the human resources and intellectual capacity to drive research and innovation but lacked a dependable legal and institutional framework to finance, coordinate and commercialise research findings. He explained that the proposed legislation was designed to bridge the gap between laboratory discoveries and their practical application in the marketplace. Zannah urged stakeholders to critically examine five major areas of the Bill, including governance and institutional structure, funding sources, grant administration and commercialisation, accountability, and potential implementation gaps. On funding, he drew attention to the proposed 20 per cent contribution from the Nigerian Content Development Fund under Section 19 of the Bill, alongside government appropriations, grants and income generated from commercialisation. item.title: NSCDC orders trial of officer over shooting of trailer driver in Gombe
item.description: ….Commandant relieves personnel of duty, orders disciplinary investigation By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Gombe State Command, has ordered an Orderly Room Trial of a personnel attached to its Anti-Vandal Unit over an alleged shooting incident involving a trailer driver along Gombe Bypass. The incident occurred on Thursday morning, November 12, 2026, at New Mile 3, during a routine enforcement operation by personnel of the unit. The State Commandant, Commandant Muhammed Inuwa Usman, gave the directive following an altercation reportedly involving the NSCDC personnel and the trailer driver, which left the driver with gunshot injuries. In response, Usman ordered the arrest of the officer allegedly involved and relieved him of his operational duties pending the conclusion of disciplinary proceedings. He also constituted a Disciplinary Committee to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident and ensure that the matter was handled thoroughly, professionally and in accordance with established procedures. The Command disclosed in a statement that the outcome of the Orderly Room Trial and the internal disciplinary process would be made public upon their conclusion. Expressing regret over the incident, Usman reaffirmed the Corps’ commitment to protecting lives and property, upholding professional standards and respecting the fundamental rights of citizens. He stressed that the Command would neither condone nor shield any personnel whose conduct endangered public safety or violated operational guidelines and established rules of engagement. The Commandant appealed to residents, motorists and other members of the public, particularly those around the Gombe Bypass, to remain calm and law-abiding while investigations continued. He also wished the injured driver a speedy recovery, assuring the public that appropriate disciplinary measures would be taken and justice pursued in accordance with the law. item.title: FG moves to abolish 269 obsolete laws as review committee submits report
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA– The Federal Government on Thursday began the process of repealing 269 laws it described as obsolete. The action followed the formal presentation of the report of the committee set up in 2024 to review all the laws in the country to the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN. The Committee, which was led by a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) and former Attorney General of Ekiti State, Mr. Olawale Fapohunda, was co-chaired by Professor Dakas Dakas, SAN. While presenting the report to the AGF at the Ministry of Justice headquarters in Abuja, Mr. Fapohunda, SAN, disclosed that the Committee considered a total of 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations. He added that, of the laws considered, 663, together with their relevant subsidiary legislations, were identified for inclusion in the Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN), while 269 were found to be obsolete, spent or repealed. Fapohunda, SAN, who noted that significant portions of laws in the country had not undergone a comprehensive, systemic review in nearly two decades, said the revised laws contained in the report of the committee will usher in a forward-looking era for Law Reform in Nigeria. “Our primary objective was clear—to purge obsolete and redundant statutes, resolve conflicting provisions, and seamlessly integrate contemporary socio-economic and technological realities into our national legal framework. “The statutory laws of any nation are the bedrock of its governance, economic stability, and social justice. However, a legal system that remains stagnant while society evolves becomes an impediment to progress. “Our Committee was confronted with laws that still referenced obsolete economic indicators, archaic penalties, and administrative frameworks that do not align with modern technological advancements or international best practices. “Our mandate was not merely to edit, but to fundamentally sanitize our statute books. “In carrying out this responsibility, the Committee took care to preserve the substance of existing laws and to distinguish between legislation that remained in force, legislation that had been repealed, legislation that had become spent, and legislation requiring further legislative attention. “To ensure a thorough and inclusive outcome, the Committee adopted a multi-layered approach: Fourteen Working Groups were constituted to undertake the detailed review of the assigned volumes of legislation, supported by Technical Teams responsible for collation, drafting, quality assurance, oversight and editorial review. “This structure was designed to ensure that the review was undertaken systematically, while providing successive levels of technical and editorial scrutiny. Particular attention was given to the need for accuracy and consistency,” the Committee Chairman added. He expressed the hope that the exercise will lay the foundation of a more regular and sustainable system of law

item.title: Ghana launches smaller, tougher banknotes to fight counterfeiting
item.description: Ghana unveiled smaller, longer-lasting banknotes on Thursday, introducing upgraded anti-counterfeiting safeguards and designs celebrating its national heritage as it modernises its currency. The central bank said the redesign was necessary because some core banknote designs have been in circulation for more than two decades, while counterfeiting technology and international security standards have evolved. Made from reinforced cotton paper, the new notes are designed to withstand frequent handling and Ghana’s tropical climate, reducing wear and the cost of replacing damaged currency. Improved tactile markings will also help people with visual impairments distinguish between notes, the bank said. They are also portable, moving towards the compact banknote formats familiar in Europe and other international markets. “The new notes are also smaller and easier to handle,” President John Mahama said at an an event where the notes were launched, describing the improvements as practical changes for everyday transactions. The so-called “Heritage Series” will enter circulation on December 1 alongside existing notes, which remain legal tender, Bank of Ghana Governor Johnson Asiama said at a ceremony in Accra. The overhaul retains eight denominations, ranging from one to 200 cedis, including the return of the two-cedi banknote. It does not change the currency’s value or amount to a redenomination. Beyond security, the new designs celebrate Ghanaian national heroes including former UN secretary-general Kofi Annan and the country’s first president Kwame Nkrumah, historic landmarks and monuments. Ghana introduced the cedi as its national currency in July 1965, eight years after gaining independence from Britain. The redesign comes as the West African nation expands digital payments, although the central bank insisted physical currency remained indispensable. “Physical cash remains an essential pillar of our monetary resilience,” Asiama said, warning that cyberattacks, technical failures and natural disasters could disrupt electronic payment networks. The central bank is also preparing legislation to replace the 1964 currency act, strengthening provisions against counterfeiting and the deliberate destruction or misuse of banknotes. item.title: Court fixes Friday for judgment in PDP, Adebutu’s suit against INEC
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja fixed Friday to deliver judgment in a suit filed by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) seeking to compel the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish the name of its candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, for the 2027 Ogun governorship election. Justice Peter Lifu fixed the date after parties called their witnesses and adopted their processes in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/2573/2026. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the PDP and Adebutu had, on Oct. 22, filed the suit following the removal of Adebutu’s name from the list of contestants of the governorship seat in Ogun. The plaintiffs sued INEC as the sole defendant in the suit filed by their lawyer, Ahmed Raji, SAN. The plaintiffs, who sought six questions for determination, prayed the court for 11 reliefs. They sought an order setting aside the commission’s decision to omit, remove or refuse to publish Adebutu’s name in the final list of candidates published on Oct. 10 for denial of a fair hearing and violation of the provisions of Section 29 and Section 32 of the Electoral Act, 2026. They also sought an order directing or compelling “the defendant to, within twenty-four (24) hours of the order/orders of this honourable court, include and/or publish the name of the 2nd plaintiff as the 1st plaintiff’s governorship candidate for Ogun State in the forthcoming 2027 General Election,” among other reliefs. In a counter-affidavit deposed to by Mr Mustapha Mohammed, a Chief Programme Analyst in its Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Department, INEC told the court that Adebutu’s name was not found in the register of members the PDP earlier submitted to it. INEC told the court that it found only the name of the PDP’s deputy governorship candidate in the state, Kolapo Lateefat Oyeyemi, in the register. Meanwhile, at the last sitting on Nov. 5, the plaintiffs and the defendants called their witnesses to testify as to the propriety of their claims. Giving his evidence on behalf of the plaintiffs, the PDP National Organising Secretary, Umar Bature, told the court that in the flash drive submitted to INEC which contained all the names of its candidates, the name of Adebutu was included. Bature, who was led in evidence by Raji, stated that contrary to the colour of the INEC’s flash drive brought to the court, the flash drive submitted to the commission was silver in colour. The PDP witness said the party only submitted a soft copy of the list of their candidates, which was the flash drive, to the electoral umpire in line with the Electoral Act and Paragraph 4(3) of Part 1 of the Regulations and Guidelines for Political Parties, 2026, issued by INEC. In his testimony, Mohammed, the Chief Programme Analyst with INEC, insisted that Adebutu’s name was not in the list of names of candidates submitted to the commission. item.title: [Photos] ‘They came in four buses’ – NDC member narrates how thugs invaded Lagos rally
item.description: *We weren’t informed of political rally – Police By Mathew Johnson It was a terrifying experience for members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, who had gathered for a town hall meeting in Oregun, Lagos, on Thursday. The event was part of the scheduled visit of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and vice, Rabiu Kwankwanso. Read Also: Video: Thugs attack NDC supporters in Lagos According to some of the supporters’ accounts, the gathering was disrupted when about 50 suspected political thugs, allegedly armed with guns, cutlasses, axes, machetes and other dangerous weapons, stormed the premises, attacking party members. The ensuing stampede sent participants scampering for safety. Recounting how the attack unfolded, one of the party members, Olamilekan Olayiwola, Ward F Chairman and security coordinator at the event, said party members had arrived at the venue as early as 8a.m. They then noticed five commercial buses – LT buses – parked outside the premises. According to him: “The incident happened as supporters were waiting for preparations at the hall to be completed ahead of Peter Obi’s arrival. “The attack started around 8a.m. Before it happened, I saw five LT buses parked outside the premises, with their occupants threatening to scatter everything. “They had guns, cutlasses and axes. They attacked us, forcing some of our members to mobilise the women to defend themselves. “Four party members sustained injuries during the clash, while several others lost their mobile phones. There was no police officer on the ground, except for two DSS operatives, who fired warning shots into the air to disperse the attackers. “I am calling on political leaders and security agencies to put adequate security arrangements in place for campaign events and polling units across Lagos State because. “If nothing is done, the situation could turn bloody.” However, at the time of time of writing this report, armed policemen numbering over 20 were sighted at the scene, while members were still waiting for Obi and Kwankwaso’s arrival. item.title: ‘I’m Here’, Fubara Declares As Wike Inaugurates Rainbow Coalition, APC Campaign Council In Rivers
item.description: The Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, on Thursday, declared his unwavering support for the All Progressives Congress (APC), stating that he is fully involved in the Rainbow Coalition movement. He made the declaration as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, inaugurated members of the Rivers APC Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in the State. He urged members to demonstrate through their actions that they are committed to the political cause ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor said he expected members to be honest about their political convictions, stressing that those unwilling to support his position should openly take a different path rather than engage in double-dealing. He said his political decision is firm and would not be different whether expressed publicly or privately. “Don’t say you’re openly with me, and behind you’re doing a different thing. I’m here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day, in private and in secret. I have taken this position, and anybody who says he is not with me, gently go your way.” Gov. Fubara also urged members to put past political differences behind them, noting that the new campaign council has brought together a broader spectrum of political stakeholders, including some who were previously in opposition. He described the expanded composition of the council as an advantage that could strengthen the coalition’s chances if members worked together. Recalling the 2023 general elections, the governor said a similar political structure had helped secure victory for him and President Bola Tinubu, expressing confidence that the new council could deliver even more votes in 2027. He challenged members to approach the assignment with determination, insisting that electoral success would depend on their willingness to work collectively towards a common objective. “If we take it as a serious responsibility, a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisive, with a stronger vote that is more than what we did in 2023.” The governor congratulated members of the inaugurated council and assured those who were not included in the initial list that additional committees would be constituted and the structure could still be expanded. He expressed appreciation to the council’s leadership and other political stakeholders for their efforts, praying for success in the task ahead. The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, speaking while inaugurating members of the Rivers APC Campaign Council and Rainbow Coalition in Rivers State on Thursday, November 12, 2026. On his three million vote projection for President Bola Tinubu, Fubara said that nothing was impossible with dedication and seriousness. item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of AI giant Nvidia on Thursday, the company said, after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor, ending Huang’s 33-year run at the helm of the global juggernaut he co-founded. Huang, 63, also gave up his seat on the board. The company did not give a reason for his departure. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion-dollar company plunging, and the exit of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom, leaves Nvidia without its founding leader at a crucial time for the sector. Nvidia shares were down more than 10 percent in premarket trading Thursday following the announcement. The stock was already down around 25 percent from its all-time high in early October. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. The board said it had appointed Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as its first-ever chair. “The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption,” Jones said in a statement. Kress said she was committed to “building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.” – Two affairs – The scandal began with reports that Huang, who has been married to Lori Huang for more than 40 years, was involved in an extramarital relationship. Jensen Huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, who was a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. On Sunday, Nvidia’s board announced a probe into what it called reporting that Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort,” while saying it retained confidence in him. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported that Huang had a second extramarital affair, citing video evidence of him being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand its technology into higher education and health care. She was speaking at a conference in San Jose, California, where the two “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. Nvidia’s code of conduct tells employees to avoid conflicts of interest and cites the example of “personal relationships.” Nvidia shareholders have filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the company for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors. – Successor search – Huang had repeatedly avoided naming a successor when the question was raised. Kress joined Nvidia as finance chief in 2013 after nearly 25 years

item.title: Photos: Bianca remembers Ojukwu on 32nd wedding anniversary
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, has paid tribute to her late husband, former Biafran leader, Chukwuemeka Odumegwu-Ojukwu, as she marked what would have been their 32nd wedding anniversary. Bianca shared a throwback photograph from their wedding ceremony on November 12, 1994, alongside an emotional message on IG on Thursday. Reflecting on their years together, she expressed gratitude for the time they shared and the memories they created. “12 November 1994, 32 years to this day. And my heart remembers the beautiful journey we shared, the love we built, the memories we created, and the promises we made,” she wrote. She added, “Grateful to God for the precious time we shared, and will continue to cherish every memory until we meet again in eternity. Happy Anniversary, my Dearest.” Chukwuemeka Odumegwu-Ojukwu, popularly known as Ikemba Nnewi, died on November 26, 2011, in the United Kingdom at the age of 78. He was the leader of the defunct Republic of Biafra during the Nigerian Civil War, which lasted from 1967 to 1970. Bianca has continued to remember her late husband on significant dates, honouring his memory years after his death. item.title: Trump says US does not ‘need a deal with Iran’
item.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that he was directing Vice President JD Vance to focus completely on domestic anti-fraud efforts and not negotiations towards a deal to end war with Tehran. “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. His comments came shortly after the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Vance was mulling face-to-face talks with a top Iranian security official. The Journal’s report added Trump had told aides and counterparts that he was open to Vance reopening talks with Tehran, and that the president had empowered Vance to negotiate. Such an in-person meeting would mark an unusual move. Oil prices rose after Trump’s remarks on social media, while Wall Street futures slipped further. Trump’s comments also come after his Republican Party were hit by sweeping losses in this month’s midterm elections, with Democrats gaining control of Congress. Anger over war with Iran, which has caused fuel prices to surge in the United States, has been seen as a key factor pushing voters away from Republicans. Vance was among Republicans to blame the Iran war for the party’s losses at the ballot box. The conflict has been ongoing since US-Israel strikes on Iran from late February, prompting Tehran to choke off the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for energy transit. The blockage has wreaked havoc on the world economy, causing energy costs to rocket. The post Trump says US does not ‘need a deal with Iran’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Seyi Tinubu gets Northern youths’ backing over Gwandu title
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja A Northern youth organisation, the Northern Youth Frontiers, Northwest Zone, has commended the conferment of a traditional title on President Bola Tinubu’s son, Seyi Tinubu, by the Emir of Gwandu, Alhaji Muhammadu Iliyasu Bashar. The group described the honour as recognition of Seyi Tinubu’s contributions to youth empowerment, community development and humanitarian activities, urging him to use the recognition as motivation to deepen his commitment to young Nigerians and national unity. Seyi Tinubu was turbaned as Dan Zaki Gwandu, meaning “Son of the Lion of Gwandu”, at the historic Abdullahi Fodiyo Palace in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State. In a congratulatory statement on Thursday, the Northwest Coordinator of the organisation, Saminu Turaki, said the honour reflected what he described as Tinubu’s contributions to youth empowerment, community development and humanitarian services across the country. Turaki described the title, reportedly the first of its kind in the history of the Gwandu Emirate, as more than a ceremonial recognition, saying it underscored the importance of service, leadership and relationships that transcend ethnic and cultural boundaries. He said the development demonstrated the enduring relationship between traditional institutions and efforts to promote national unity, noting that traditional rulers remained important custodians of Nigeria’s cultural heritage and social cohesion. “This historic honour reflects the enduring bonds of friendship, mutual respect and national unity among Nigeria’s diverse peoples, highlighting the critical role traditional institutions play as custodians of our culture and national cohesion,” he said. The group also expressed solidarity with Seyi Tinubu as he assumes the responsibilities associated with the traditional title, expressing confidence that he would uphold the values of courage, humility, leadership and selfless service. “We are confident that he will embody the core values of courage, leadership, humility and selfless service associated with this esteemed title. We encourage him to let this honour further inspire his commitment to empowering young Nigerians and promoting peaceful coexistence,” Turaki said. The organisation urged the new Dan Zaki Gwandu to use the recognition as an opportunity to expand initiatives that create opportunities for young people and promote peaceful coexistence across the country. It also wished him wisdom, strength and divine guidance in discharging the responsibilities associated with the traditional honour and serving humanity and the nation. item.title: Migration to developed countries declines for second year – OECD
item.description: Migration to developed countries dwindled for a second year in a row in 2025, down 1.6 percent compared to the previous year, according to an OECD report published Thursday. While still experiencing high numbers, the 38 Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries recorded 6.1 million new permanent immigrants in 2025, compared to 6.2 million the previous year. There has been a backlash in many Western countries against the arrival of irregular migrants fleeing conflict, authoritarian rule and economic hardship in their home countries. Legal humanitarian migration dropped “sharply” by 26 percent in 2025 compared with 2024, the report found. Labour migration increased by 13 percent. While 2025 marked an overall decline in migration, the number of permanent immigrants settling for the long term was up 12 percent compared with 2019. Three countries recorded a notable spike in permanent migrants in 2025. Portugal saw a 139-percent increase to 313,600 individuals, resulting from approvals of a backlog of pending residency permits. Spain saw a 25-percent increase to 460,500 people, notably after having broadened its residency policies. Italy saw a 45-percent increase to 248,800 people, largely attributed to a flux of family and labour migration. Other countries saw significant declines in permanent migrants. The United States saw a 14-percent drop, although it still leads OECD countries, recording more than 1.2 million permanent migrants in 2025. Canada saw a 19-percent decrease to 393,800 people, and the United Kingdom a 32 percent decline to 295,800 people. – Asylum seekers down – India remained the leading country of origin for migratory flows to the OECD in 2024, ahead of China and Colombia, according to the latest available figures. The 1.1 million asylum applications in 2025 marked a 22-percent decrease to OECD countries, excluding the United States, compared with the previous year, although remaining about 10 percent higher than 2019 figures. Men continue to account for the majority of migratory flows to OECD countries. According to the latest available data from 2024, women accounted for about 46 percent of new immigrants. The OECD countries that admitted significantly more women than men were the United States and Ireland with 54 percent female immigrants; Sweden with 53 percent, and Israel, Chile, Australia and New Zealand with 52 percent. Migration poses an opportunity to boost long-term productivity in many countries, particularly in the face of aging populations, the OECD noted. “With the OECD working-age population set to decrease by 8 percent by 2060, pushing overall growth downwards, reviving productivity growth is key to maintaining living standards,” said Mark Pearson, the OECD’s acting director of Employment, Labour and Social Affairs. “Immigrants now account for 16 percent of employment across the OECD, 3 percentage points more than a decade ago,” he added. item.title: 2027: Otti flags off LP campaign in Imo, urges vote protection
item.description: By Steve Oko Abia State Governor and National Leader of the Labour Party (LP), Dr Alex Otti, has expressed confidence that the party will record significant victories in the 2027 elections in Imo State, urging its candidates to intensify grassroots mobilisation and protect their votes. Otti, who travelled to Owerri to flag off the party’s campaign in the state, challenged candidates and supporters to approach the electoral contest with courage, determination and vigilance, stressing that winning elections required more than merely casting ballots. The governor spoke at All Saints Cathedral Church Field, Egbu, Owerri, during the campaign flag-off attended by the party’s national leadership, candidates and supporters. Addressing the gathering, Otti urged the candidates to approach the elections with the conviction that victory was achievable, warning that failure to protect their votes could undermine their efforts. “Go out there and win because victory is certain. “You have only one vote. Only one. So, it is not enough to cast it; you need to protect it,” he said. He congratulated the candidates on securing the party’s tickets and urged them to close ranks, strengthen grassroots mobilisation and work collectively towards electoral success. Otti, however, clarified that the Imo governorship seat was not part of the contest, disclosing that the incumbent governor, Hope Uzodimma, was his close friend. He cautioned against political comparisons and the indiscriminate chanting of “Best Governor”, noting that every state had its peculiar challenges and required a distinct approach to governance. According to him, his administration in Abia was focused on addressing the challenges inherited on assumption of office rather than competing with other governors. The LP National Chairman, Senator Nenadi Usman, represented by the Deputy National Chairman, Hon. Salisu Nuhu Muhammed, formally presented the party’s flags to its candidates for Imo East Senatorial District and other National and State Assembly constituencies. Usman charged the candidates to carry the party’s flags with pride and work towards victory, expressing confidence that the LP would make significant electoral gains in Imo State. She also urged voters in Imo East to support the party, describing Otti’s performance in Abia as evidence of the LP’s capacity to deliver good governance. The party’s National Secretary, Hon. Acho Obioma; National Organising Secretary, Mrs Oluchi Opara; National Woman Leader, Mrs Hilda Dokubo; and National Youth Leader, Hon. Collins Okpara, also rallied support for the candidates. They commended Otti’s leadership and urged voters in Imo East and other constituencies to give the party an opportunity, expressing optimism that it could replicate developments in Abia if entrusted with power. The LP senatorial candidate for Imo East, Sir Basil Maduka, thanked Otti for attending the rally, describing his presence as a demonstration of solidarity with the candidates. Maduka

item.title: Navy dismantles illegal refineries, recovers 53,000 litres in Rivers
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Navy has dismantled two illegal refining sites and recovered 53,000 litres of suspected stolen petroleum products in Okarki community, Ahoada West Local Government Area of Rivers State. The operation, conducted on November 11, 2026, was carried out by the Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Pathfinder under Operation Delta Sentinel, following credible intelligence on illegal petroleum activities in the area. The Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, disclosed this on Thursday, saying the operation underscored the Navy’s determination to combat crude oil theft and illegal bunkering. According to him, the two sites contained about eight dugout pits and storage containers holding an estimated 23,000 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and 30,000 litres of suspected illegally refined Automotive Gas Oil (AGO). He said the sites and recovered products were handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures. Folorunsho, however, disclosed that no arrests were made because the suspected operators fled before the arrival of the naval team. He said the operation reinforced the Navy’s sustained efforts to dismantle illegal refining infrastructure and disrupt networks involved in crude oil theft. The naval spokesman recalled that NNS Pathfinder had conducted an earlier operation in the same general area on October 10, 2026, during which three illegal refining sites were discovered and deactivated. He said the successive operations demonstrated the Navy’s resolve to deny economic saboteurs access to the nation’s petroleum resources. Folorunsho reaffirmed the Navy’s commitment to sustaining intelligence-led operations under Operation Delta Sentinel to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure, support national crude oil production and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. item.title: UNIJOS Appoints First Female Vice Chancellor In 50-Year History
item.description: The University of Jos has appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the establishment of the institution. Her appointment was announced on Thursday by the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the University’s Governing Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent, during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council. Professor Lar takes over from Professor Tanko Ishaya, whose tenure as Vice Chancellor has come to an end. Presenting the letter of appointment to the incoming Vice Chancellor, Senator Bent charged her to remain focused in the discharge of her responsibilities as she prepares to lead the university. Her emergence marks a historic milestone for the University of Jos, as she becomes the first female Vice Chancellor in the institution’s history and the 11th substantive head of the university. item.title: Money Laundering: Court sends Maina’s son to prison to begin seven-year term
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — Following his rearrest by security operatives after he was convicted in absentia, the Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday remanded Faisal, son of the jailed former Chairman of the defunct Pension Reform Taskforce Team (PRTT), Abdulrasheed Maina, in prison. The court, in a ruling delivered by Justice James Omotosho, held that Faisal, who was found guilty of money laundering, should be sent to the Kuje correctional facility to commence his seven-year jail term. It will be recalled that Faisal, who is 26 years old, was convicted and sentenced to 14 years in prison by the high court on October 7, 2021. The court, in the judgment delivered by trial Justice Okon Abang, found the convict guilty on all three counts of money laundering charges that the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) preferred against him. The convict, who jumped bail on June 24, 2020, failed to appear in court for the conclusion of his trial. The EFCC told the court that it got intelligence that he had escaped to the United States of America (USA). The trial court ordered that he should be arrested whenever he was found in the country and remanded in any prison to serve his jail term. It held that the Federal Government should, upon confirming that he had run outside the country, “legally or lawfully commence extradition process to bring him into the country to serve the jail term.” Dissatisfied with the judgment, the convict’s lawyers went before the appellate court to set it aside. They argued that Faisal had been denied fair hearing by the trial court. In its own judgment on November 24, 2022, a three-member panel of the appellate court upheld Faisal’s conviction but described the 14-year jail term handed to him by the trial court as “excessive.” It noted that the appellant, being a first-time offender, should not have been handed the maximum punishment prescribed by the law. Consequently, the appellate court, in its lead judgment delivered by Justice Ugochukwu Ogakwu, reduced Faisal’s term of imprisonment to seven years. The convict was later arrested this year after he allegedly sneaked into the country, about four years after he was sentenced in absentia. The EFCC approached the court with an ex parte motion seeking a warrant committing the convict to prison to serve his sentence. The commission also requested that his prison term commence from October 14, 2026, when he was rearrested by the Department of State Services (DSS) in the Karsana area of Abuja. The application, which was moved by EFCC counsel M.K. Hussain, was granted by the court. Justice Omotosho held that the convict should serve three years’ imprisonment on count one, seven years on count two and three years on count three, in accordance with the Court of Appeal’s verdict. He held that the sentences should run concurrently, starting from October 14. The trial court had, in its verdict, held that the EFCC successfully established that Faisal operated a fictitious bank

item.title: Obidient Movement congratulates Yunusa Tanko on appointment as SDP presidential campaign DG
item.description: The Obidient Movement has congratulated its former National Coordinator, Dr Yunusa Tanko, on his appointment as National Coordinator of the Social Democratic Party’s Presidential Campaign Council ahead of the 2027 general elections. The movement described the appointment as recognition of Tanko’s political experience, organisational skills and contributions to the struggle for a better Nigeria. In a statement issued on Wednesday by its Media and Communications Directorate, the group wished him success in his new role, saying his emergence reflected the leadership capacity developed within the movement. It said Tanko’s appointment, despite his move to a different political platform, should be seen as an opportunity for collaboration rather than a source of division. The movement explained that its membership extended beyond party lines, bringing together Nigerians from different ethnic, religious and social backgrounds around the shared aspiration for competent and accountable leadership. While encouraging its members to join the Nigeria Democratic Congress, the party of its principal, Peter Obi, it said it recognised that its supporters belonged to different political parties. “Consequently, the emergence of leaders from our Movement into influential positions across different political platforms should be a source of pride, not division,” the statement said. The group also cited Obi’s attendance at the inauguration of the presidential campaign office of Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, as an example of his belief in cooperation across political differences. According to the movement, Obi has consistently maintained that national interest should take precedence over partisan considerations. It added that its objective was not to confine capable Nigerians to one political party but to develop leaders who could contribute to national development wherever they found themselves. Tanko was on Wednesday unveiled as the SDP’s national presidential campaign coordinator during the inauguration of the party’s campaign council in Abuja. He pledged to work with the party’s presidential candidate, Adewale Adebayo, and his running mate, Usman Bugaje, ahead of the 2027 elections. The appointment followed Tanko’s resignation as political adviser (North) to Obi, which he said took effect on October 30. item.title: Suspected Thugs Attack NDC Supporters In Lagos Ahead Of Peter Obi’s Town Hall
item.description: Suspected political thugs on Thursday, November 12, 2026, attacked members and supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Oregun area of Ikeja, Lagos State, disrupting preparations for a town hall meeting scheduled to be addressed by the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. The incident, which occurred around 11:00 a.m. at the Classique Event Centre along Kudirat Abiola Way, sent scores of attendees scampering for safety and triggered panic in the surrounding commercial district. Motorists plying Kudirat Abiola Way were forced to make abrupt U-turns to avoid the melee, while pedestrians fled the area. Crowd of NDC supporters gather outside town hall after attack by thugs. According to witnesses at the scene, neither Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, nor Kwankwaso, a former governor of Kano State, had arrived at the venue when the attackers struck. Shattered glass on the floor, as captured by our reporter at the scene of the disrupted town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Oregun, Lagos State, on Thursday, November 12, 2026 : Nosakhale Akhimien/Channels TV https://t.co/lR2QKFNf8v — Channels Television (@channelstv) November 12, 2026 Shattered glass littered the floor of the disrupted venue, while several vehicles belonging to NDC members and supporters stood vandalised within the premises. One party supporter, speaking to Channels Television after sustaining a head injury, alleged that hoodlums armed with cutlasses invaded the area in an attempt to derail the gathering. He noted that additional NDC members were mobilised to resist the assailants, eventually forcing them to retreat. “When I arrived out here, we reacted to our president without fear. They started fighting back, breaking our vehicles, and destroying property,” the injured supporter told Channels Television, adding that attendees retaliated in self-defence despite being outnumbered and warning of heightened tensions ahead of the 2027 elections. ﻿ Armed policemen and security patrol vehicles were subsequently deployed to the Classique Event Centre to restore order and prevent further escalation. Following the arrival of law enforcement, the atmosphere gradually stabilised, with NDC supporters seen dancing, singing, and defiantly raising the party’s flag as they awaited the arrival of their presidential ticket. The NDC governorship candidate in Lagos State, Funso Doherty, also arrived at the venue to assess the extent of the damage. A supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is seen raising the party’s flag at the venue of the party’s town hall meeting in the Oregun area of Lagos State on Thursday, November 12, 2026. item.title: ACF crisis deepens
item.description: Moves to resolve the lingering supremacy battle within the ranks of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) have yet to produce results after a closed-door meeting by members of the Board of Trustees (BoT), the National Executive Committee (NEC) and some first-class emirs from the northern region ended in what some sources described as “deadlock.” Daily Trust learnt that the meeting, which took place on Tuesday at the private residence of the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III, in Maitama, Abuja, lasted two hours between 5pm and 7pm without any tangible resolutions reached. The traditional rulers at the meeting included the Etsu Nupe, Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar, and the Aku Uka of Wukari, Dr. Manu Ishaku Adda Ali. The Sultan was reportedly not at the meeting as he was attending to other matters of national importance somewhere. Although the details of the meeting, which was convened at the instance of the Sultan, were sketchy, sources privy to the happenings in the ACF confided in Daily Trust that the gathering focused on resolving the worsening division in the leadership of the northern socio-political group. One of the sources said both the Etsu Nupe and the Aku Uka expressed serious reservations over the inability of the BoT and NEC to arrive at a neutral ground and work together towards finding solution to the security and economic challenges afflicting the North. “In fact, one of the emirs alluded to the fact that the North is now a laughing stock…That we cannot speak with one voice at a critical moment of our existence,” he said. Our correspondents report that the meeting on Tuesday was a continuation of series of engagements with contending parties (NEC and BoT) towards resolving the protracted leadership crisis occasioned by alleged financial impropriety. Daily Trust learnt that the Sultan, with the support of the Emir of Lafia, Justice Sidi Dauda Bage Muhammad and other northern traditional rulers have been having talks with the ACF leaders since the beginning of 2026 when the BoT and NEC engaged in blame game. On one hand, the Chairman of the BoT, Alhaji Bashir Dalhatu, with the support of some members, had asked the Secretary General of the organisation, Malam Murtala Aliyu, to leave. But Murtala had kicked saying his tenure will expire in December 2026. He reportedly has the support of some members, including the Chairman of the NEC, Barrister Mamman Mike Osuman, SAN. Besides the leadership tussle, the lodgement of about N3.9 billion donated to the ACP in a new account at JAIZ Bank, rather than in any of the main accounts of the organisation in First Bank, United Bank for Africa (UBA) and Unity Bank, has caused disaffection among members. During its 25th anniversary celebration held in November 2025, some notable northern leaders and businessmen donated the amount, in addition to pledges that are yet to be redeemed.
